rows.snippet: their position in the mother cell determines which offspring inherits the inclusion body and where it will be located within it
rows.section: Results: Inclusion Bodies Are Formed in Discrete Cellular Positions and Accumulate in Old Poles Under Nonstressing Conditions
rows.notes: Lindner et al. 2008, PMID:18287048. Primary PMC Results and Methods directly read. The quoted position is that of an IbpA-YFP focus. MGAY is an engineered MG1655 reporter strain, grown on LB-agarose at 37 C without imposed stress. Figure 2 is the inspected localization measurement; Figure 3 is an inspected lineage schematic, not another experiment. Pole identity changes across divisions. The observations support inheritance and eventual older-pole accumulation; they do not establish active transport, universal aggregate toxicity or a natural canonical exemplar. Supplements were not inspected.
rows.title: Asymmetric segregation of protein aggregates is associated with cellular aging and rejuvenation.

rows.snippet: We experimentally confirmed that fusion increases segregation asymmetry, for a range of stresses, and identified Hsp16 as a fusion factor.
rows.notes: Coelho et al. 2014, PMID:24936793. Hsp104-GFP fission-yeast imaging supports stress-associated unequal inheritance without consistent old/new-pole bias. Actual Figures 3, 4 and S4 were inspected. Figure 3C measures an absolute sibling difference in aggregate-associated fluorescence, not concentration; S4I measures count asymmetry. Figure 4B is fusion and 4C is nucleation: the caption reverses them. A Results pointer to 4C for stress-dependent asymmetry disagrees with the plotted endpoints. Figure 3C describes continuous 40 C, whereas Methods describes 40 C for one hour followed by 37 C; this remains unresolved. Text S1 experimental methods and strain table were text-extracted, not visually rendered. No universal transport, death threshold or rejuvenation mechanism is inferred.
rows.title: Fusion of protein aggregates facilitates asymmetric damage segregation.

rows.snippet: Noticeably, stalked cells always inherited more aggregates (75%) than swarmer cells (25%).
rows.section: Results: The aggregate load does not sort to swarmer or stalked daughter cells in C. crescentus
rows.notes: Schramm et al. 2019, PMID:30779464. Primary XML Results, Discussion and relevant Methods were read; actual Figure 6 was inspected. DnaK-mVenus, delta-clpB cells recovered at 30 C after 10 minutes at 40 C. Figure 6G reports aggregate allocation across daughter cell types over successive divisions, not the fraction of all sibling pairs with unequal counts. Figure 6F measures projected cell area, not volume. Unequal shared inheritance is compatible with the proposed broad phenotype; it contradicts neither sharing nor a stable allocation ratio. The paper limits universal exclusive old-pole retention, not every form of quantitative inequality. Supplements and independent strain provenance were not inspected; no natural canonical example is asserted.
rows.title: Growth-driven displacement of protein aggregates along the cell length ensures partitioning to both daughter cells in Caulobacter crescentus.

candidate.working_label: unequal protein aggregate inheritance at cell division
candidate.draft_definition: A physiological phenotype in which division of a microbial cell produces sibling cells with unequal numbers or amounts of inherited protein aggregates.
candidate.scope_decision_still_needed: Confirm the utility of a qualitative phenotype for reproducibly observed unequal cargo apportionment. Do not infer a taxon-level trait from one random sibling split, aggregate presence, reporter-gene presence, or cell size alone. Preserve each assay's count/amount scale and baseline; do not invent a universal threshold or require a fixed lineage bias.
candidate.synonym_policy: Do not automatically treat asymmetric damage segregation, old-pole retention, aggregate exclusion, protein aggregation or rejuvenation as exact synonyms. A source may use asymmetric segregation more narrowly than numerical inequality.
candidate.mechanism_policy: First-pass protein examples, canonical taxa, xrefs and causal graphs should remain absent unless separately supported and authority-checked. Reporter/deletion experiments support qualified observations, not natural canonical strain status. No universal active transport, Hsp16 dependence, aggregate toxicity, aging or rejuvenation is implied.

corrected_precuration_interpretations.finding: Shared inheritance is not necessarily equal inheritance.
corrected_precuration_interpretations.disposition: The Caulobacter study is not a categorical negative for a broad unequal-apportionment phenotype. Its measured shared unequal allocation limits universal exclusive old-pole retention. Figure 6G percentages are aggregate allocation across cell types, not the proportion of sibling pairs with unequal counts; Figure 6F uses projected cell area, not volume.

corrected_precuration_interpretations.finding: The fission-yeast figure caption cannot be used to infer panel identity without the image.
corrected_precuration_interpretations.disposition: Both publisher and PMC Figure 4 were inspected: B measures fusion and C nucleation, contrary to the caption. Figure 3C and Figure 4G address amount asymmetry; Figure 4H addresses aggregate-free offspring. Keep the separate continuous-heat discrepancy between Figure 3C and Methods explicit.
